name: dsh-evolve
description: Self-evolving memory + skill lifecycle for DeepSeek Harness. Structured cross-session memory (Culeot-style, MIT) with deterministic zero-token recall (bigram-Jaccard fused with FTS5 BM25 via RRF) + JSON truth + Markdown mirror + git checkpoints + human-approval gate. Skills crystallize into SKILL.md, REFINE in place over time (versioned, human-edit-preserving, zero extra LLM), and are curated through a real active→stale→archived lifecycle (reversible archive, never deletes) — all loaded/managed by DSH's own skill-filesystem (zero extra tokens).
comment_deps: These @deepseek-ai/* are host-provided shared packages. dshmarket's diagnostics.ts (diagnosePackageManifests → inspectKnownHostDependencyDeclarations) ONLY scans the `dependencies` field for its KNOWN_SHARED_HOST_PACKAGES list (cordis, dsh-attachment, dsh-llm, dsh-system-prompt, dsh-tools) and warns 'may shadow host'. Declaring them in devDependencies clears that warning while STILL installing local copies — which ESM import needs, because dsh boots plugins via await import WITHOUT --preserve-symlinks: the profile symlink is realpath'd to this source dir, and module resolution then walks node_modules from HERE. peerDependencies would NOT install copies → ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND at boot (verified 2026-08-20). cordis 4.x passes services via runtime ctx (not instanceof), so a local copy is not a real shadow — proven by another local plugin running a different cache's cordis copy against the host with no issue, and by driving apply under the host's real instances (all 7 tools registered).
